nodes.title: Keep the cart in one signal
nodes.why: Every cart line and its quantity live in this one array; the totals, the empty message and the cart rows all read it, so one replacement updates them together.
nodes.alternative: Keep a plain cartItems array plus separate total fields that every handler updates by hand.
nodes.tradeoff: One signal is a single source of truth that works with OnPush, at the cost of copying the array on each change; hand-kept totals are one forgotten update away from drifting.

nodes.title: Derive both totals from the lines

anchor.snippet: readonly totalQty = computed(() => this.cartItems().reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.quantity, 0));

nodes.why: totalQty and totalPrice reduce over cartItems() and recompute only when the signal receives a new array, so the header can never disagree with the rows.
nodes.alternative: Store totalQty and totalPrice as fields and adjust them inside addToCart, increaseQty, decreaseQty and removeItem.
nodes.tradeoff: Each reduce walks every line after a change, which is trivial for a few lines; stored totals skip that pass but must be kept in step by four methods.

nodes.title: Merge repeat adds into one line
nodes.why: Adding a product that is already in the cart raises that line's quantity through changeQuantity instead of appending a second line with the same id.
nodes.alternative: Append a new line on every click and group duplicates by id when rendering or totalling.
nodes.tradeoff: The some() check scans the cart on each add, but every product id stays on exactly one line, which keeps @for tracking by item.id valid.

nodes.title: Remove the line when minus reaches zero
nodes.why: Minus on a line with quantity 1 calls removeItem, so the cart never holds a line that shows a quantity of 0.
nodes.alternative: Clamp the quantity at 1 and let only the Remove button delete a line.
nodes.tradeoff: Removing at zero matches what the minus click asks for, but one accidental click drops the line; clamping is safer and makes Remove the only way out.

nodes.title: Change a quantity by copying one line

anchor.snippet: items.map((line) => (line.id === id ? { ...line, quantity: line.quantity + delta } : line))

nodes.why: Only the line with the matching id becomes a new object inside a new array, so the signal notifies and both totals recompute while the other lines keep their identity.
nodes.alternative: Find the line and change line.quantity in place, which keeps the same array and leaves the computed totals on their cached values.
nodes.tradeoff: map allocates a fresh array on every plus or minus click, a few small objects at cart size, and in return every quantity change reaches the computed totals and the OnPush view.
